title: Ensure brute-force lockout is set to 3 attempts with a lockout duration of at least 1 hour
description: FlashArray supports controls to prevent brute-force guessing of passwords. These controls cause a user to be locked out after a configurable number of consecutive failed password attempts. The lockout lasts for a configurable duration of time. Everpure recommends the following: Passes when the management password policy shows Maximum Login Attempts 1-3 and Lockout Duration of at least 60 minutes (60m, 1h, 1d or the equivalent seconds/milliseconds). The audit is a config_regex check against a text export of the Purity//FA CLI, supplied with --device-config. Capture it over SSH with the --nvp (name=value) output option, for example: ssh pureuser@<array> "purepolicy password list --nvp" > flasharray.txt (one file may hold the output of all commands used by this pack).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.6 Ensure brute-force lockout is set to 3 attempts with a lockout duration of at least 1 hour

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, configure the global password policy to enforce brute-force lockout protections and ensure the policy is actively enabled. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Settings > Access > Password Policy. ; Modify the password policy settings: set the Maximum Login Attempts to 3 and the Lockout Duration to 60 (minutes). ; Ensure the policy is toggled to Enabled and click Save. (Note: If a legitimate administrator is inadvertently locked out, you must unlock their account manually from the CLI, as there is no specific GUI toggle documented for unlocking accounts in 6.9.x). From the CLI:

title: Ensure the password policy enforces 8+ characters, 3+ character groups, and username and dictionary checks
description: FlashArray supports a password policy for administrative user passwords. It allows rules to be configured governing complexity requirements, such as minimum length, number of required unique character groups (e.g. letters, numbers, symbols), and whether a user's username may appear in their password. Passes when the password policy shows Minimum Password Length 8 or more, Minimum Character Groups 3 or more, and Enforce Dictionary Check and Enforce Username Check True. The audit is a config_regex check against a text export of the Purity//FA CLI, supplied with --device-config. Capture it over SSH with the --nvp (name=value) output option, for example: ssh pureuser@<array> "purepolicy password list --nvp" > flasharray.txt (one file may hold the output of all commands used by this pack).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.7 Ensure the password policy enforces 8+ characters, 3+ character groups, and username and dictionary checks

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, configure the global password policy to mandate longer passwords, require multiple character groups, and prevent the use of easily guessable dictionary words or usernames. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Settings > Access > Password Policy. ; Set the Minimum Password Length to 8 (or more). ; Set the Minimum Character Groups to 3. ; Ensure the toggles for Enforce Username Check and Enforce Dictionary Check are enabled. ; Click Save. From the CLI: ; Configure Length and Complexity: Set the minimum password length and character group requirements using the purepolicy password setattr command.

title: Ensure NFS export policies restrict client access and enforce secure authentication (no wildcards, root squash, no sys auth)
description: NFS Export Policies are used to control access to any given file system export over any version of the NFS protocol. They can set properties such as permitted authentication mechanisms, allowance of root access from clients, and read-only vs. read-write based on client network identity. Fails when an NFS export rule uses the * client, auth_sys security or no-root-squash; confirm krb5i/krb5p and explicit client subnets. Note: a * client in any exported rule list (SMB included) also fails this check. The audit is a config_regex check against a text export of the Purity//FA CLI, supplied with --device-config. Capture it over SSH with the --nvp (name=value) output option, for example: ssh pureuser@<array> "purepolicy nfs rule list --nvp" > flasharray.txt (one file may hold the output of all commands used by this pack).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1 Ensure NFS export policies restrict client access and enforce secure authentication (no wildcards, root squash, no sys auth)

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, update your NFS export policy rules to constrain client IPs, enforce root squash, and require Kerberos security. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Storage > Policies. ; In the Export Policies panel, click the name of the NFS policy to modify. ; In the Rules panel, click the + (Create Rule) icon to add a new, secure rule. (Note: Modifying existing NFS rules via the GUI is done by adding a new rule and removing the non-compliant one). ; Set the Client field to a specific IP subnet (e.g., 192.168.10.0/24). ; Select root-squash for the Access level. ; Select NFSv4 for the Version. ; Select krb5p (or krb5i) for Security, and ensure auth_sys is unchecked.

title: Ensure SMB client policies require encryption, restrict client access, and disable anonymous access
description: SMB Client Policies are used to control access to any given file system export over any version of the SMB protocol. They can set properties such as SMB encryption requirements, and read-only vs. read-write based on client network identity. Fails when an SMB client rule uses the * client, does not require SMB encryption, or allows anonymous access. Note: a * client in any exported rule list (NFS included) also fails this check. The audit is a config_regex check against a text export of the Purity//FA CLI, supplied with --device-config. Capture it over SSH with the --nvp (name=value) output option, for example: ssh pureuser@<array> "purepolicy smb rule list --nvp" > flasharray.txt (one file may hold the output of all commands used by this pack).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.2 Ensure SMB client policies require encryption, restrict client access, and disable anonymous access

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, update your SMB client policy rules to constrain client IPs, require SMB encryption, and ensure anonymous access remains disabled. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Storage > Policies. ; In the Export Policies panel, click the name of the SMB policy to modify. ; In the Rules panel, click the + (Create Rule) icon to add a new, secure rule. (Note: Modifying existing SMB rules via the GUI is done by adding a new rule and removing the non-compliant one). ; Set the Client field to a specific IP subnet (e.g., 192.168.10.0/24). ; Ensure the SMB Encryption Required toggle is enabled (blue). ; Ensure the Anonymous Access Allowed toggle is disabled (gray).

title: Ensure manual eradication is disabled and the eradication delay is at least 8 days for production data
description: FlashArray possesses a variety of configurations, such as realms and pods, that pertain to data protection. These configurations can have their data eradication properties configured. Everpure recommends the following: ; Disable manual eradication for all pods, realms, or arrays that will contain production data. Passes when the Disabled Delay is 8 days or more and Manual Eradication is all-disabled or partially-disabled (SafeMode in effect). The audit is a config_regex check against a text export of the Purity//FA CLI, supplied with --device-config. Capture it over SSH with the --nvp (name=value) output option, for example: ssh pureuser@<array> "purearray eradication-config list --nvp" > flasharray.txt (one file may hold the output of all commands used by this pack).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1 Ensure manual eradication is disabled and the eradication delay is at least 8 days for production data

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, extend the disabled eradication delay to at least 8 days and engage SafeMode retention locks to disable manual eradication. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Settings > System. ; In the Eradication Configuration panel, click the edit icon in the upper right corner. ; Set the Disabled Delay to at least 8 days (14 days is mathematically recommended to provide a 2-week buffer). ; Click Save. ; To actively disable manual eradication, you must enable SafeMode retention locks on your data.

title: Ensure a management SAML SSO configuration is created and enabled
description: Purity can be integrated with an external identity provider (IDP) that supports SAML. This allows for single-sign-on (SSO) functionality in the Everpure Web UI, with user provisioning, authentication, and authorization being controlled by the IDP. Everpure recommends that you create and enable a management SAML configuration. Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1 Ensure a management SAML SSO configuration is created and enabled

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Run the command puresso saml2 list to display configured SAML providers. ; Review the output to confirm that a SAML provider is present and its enabled status is True. ; Run the command puresso saml2 list --verification-certificate to view the full verification certificate details and verify the certificate issuer and expiry date. ; Test the configuration: Run the command puresso saml2 test [IDP-NAME] to verify the array URL correctness, IdP connectivity, directory service correctness, and verification certificate validity.

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, configure the array as a Service Provider (SP), exchange metadata or certificates with your Identity Provider, and rigorously test the configuration before enabling SSO. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Settings > Access > Users and Policies and scroll to the SAML2 SSO pane. ; Click the + (Create SAML2 SSO) icon. ; In the Name field, enter a local display name for the SAML2 SSO configuration. ; In the Array URL field, enter the FlashArray URL using HTTPS. ; Enter either the IdP Metadata URL, or manually enter the IdP Entity ID, IdP URL, and click Edit next to Verification Certificate to paste your IdP's PEM- formatted token-signing certificate.

title: Ensure a management LDAP/Active Directory service is configured and enabled with at least one group mapped
description: If your environment does not support SAML, Purity can be integrated with an external identity provider (IDP) that supports LDAP. This allows for password login functionality in the Everpure Web UI and CLI, with user provisioning, password management, and authorization being controlled by the IDP. Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2 Ensure a management LDAP/Active Directory service is configured and enabled with at least one group mapped

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Run the command pureds list management (or pureds list) to display the current directory service configuration. Verify the URI, Base DN, and Bind User fields are correct and the service is enabled. ; Run the command pureds role list to confirm that role-group mappings are securely defined for array roles. ; Test the configuration: Run the command pureds test to verify that the array can successfully resolve the URIs, bind to the directory using the credentials, and locate the mapped groups without errors.

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, configure the management directory service with your LDAP/AD server parameters, map your directory groups to Purity//FA roles, and rigorously test the connection before enabling it. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Settings > Access > Users and Policies. ; In the Directory Service panel, select the Array Management button, then click the edit icon. ; Enter your LDAP server URIs (using ldaps:// for encrypted connections), Base DN, Bind User, and Bind Password. Click Save. ; In the Roles section of the panel, click the edit icon.

title: Ensure only authorized local administrative accounts exist and a local emergency-access account is retained
description: If your environment does not possess any mechanisms for delegated account management, or you have a need for additional local accounts for use as service accounts or for handling administration during network outages, FlashArray supports creating additional local administrative accounts. Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3 Ensure only authorized local administrative accounts exist and a local emergency-access account is retained

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Run the command pureadmin list to enumerate all local administrator accounts. ; Review the output to confirm each account has a documented business justification and is actively required.

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, delete any local user accounts that are no longer authorized to access the FlashArray. Always ensure you maintain at least one local emergency access account with array_admin privileges in the event directory services or SAML become unavailable. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Settings > Access > Users and Policies. ; In the Users panel, click the Edit (three vertical dots) icon for the user account you want to remove and select Delete User.... ; In the Delete User pop-up window, click Delete to confirm. From the CLI: ; Delete an unauthorized or stale account using the pureadmin delete command. ; Command Syntax: pureadmin delete <USERNAME>

title: Ensure administrators and directory groups are granted least- privilege roles via management access policies
description: FlashArray provides utilities for role based access controls, with 4 built-in management access policies, which can be assigned to administrators, directory service groups, or as the maximum role that can be granted by OAuth API Clients. Management access policies may be dynamically created, allowing you to grant users different roles in different scopes (e.g. Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.4 Ensure administrators and directory groups are granted least- privilege roles via management access policies

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Run the command pureadmin list to display all local administrators. ; Review the Access Policy column in the output to confirm that each account has the appropriate minimum-privilege policy attached (and no account is unnecessarily set to array_admin). ; Run the command pureds role list to display the current LDAP/AD group to Purity//FA access policy mappings and verify their assignments. ; Run purepolicy management-access list to inspect the permissions, scopes, and aggregation strategies of all configured access policies.

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, assign users and groups the minimum role needed to accomplish their responsibilities by leveraging Purity//FA's built-in or custom Management Access Policies. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Settings > Access > Users and Policies. ; For Local Users: In the Users panel, click the edit (three vertical dots) icon for the user account and select Change Access Policy. Remove any overly permissive policies and assign the appropriate minimum-privilege policy. ; For Directory Service Groups: In the Directory Service panel, click the edit icon in the Roles section.

title: Ensure SSH key-based authentication is configured for CLI access, preferably sourced from LDAP
description: FlashArray allows for SSH public keys to be retrieved from a configurable attribute within a configured LDAP server if delegated account management with LDAP is in use. If this is not viable in your environment, or local administrative accounts are in use, then SSH public key based authentication can be configured locally per-user. Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.5 Ensure SSH key-based authentication is configured for CLI access, preferably sourced from LDAP

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Run the command pureadmin list --publickey to display all users and their public key status. ; Review the output to confirm that all authorized CLI users have a public key configured. ; Test the configuration: Initiate an SSH connection to the array from an administrative workstation using the user's private key to ensure successful authentication.

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, configure SSH public keys for your administrative accounts so they can authenticate securely using a private key rather than a password. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Settings > Access > Users and Policies. ; In the Users panel, click the Edit (three vertical dots) icon for the user you want to modify and select Edit User.... ; In the Edit User pop-up window, select Overwrite and paste the user's SSH public key into the Public Key field. ; Click Save. From the CLI: ; Add a public key: Initiate the configuration for a specific user using the pureadmin setattr command. ; Command Syntax: pureadmin setattr --publickey <USERNAME>

title: Ensure OAuth API clients use least-privilege access policies and access-token TTLs of 60 minutes or less
description: FlashArray supports configuring one or more identity providers for API Clients. These IDPs can then issue identity tokens to any user on the array that can be exchanged with the array for API access using the OAuth2 standard. Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.8 Ensure OAuth API clients use least-privilege access policies and access-token TTLs of 60 minutes or less

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Run the command pureapiclient list to display all configured API clients. ; Review the output to verify the Access Policy, Enabled status, and token TTL for each client. ; Verify no API clients are enabled that are no longer actively in use.

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, delete or disable inactive API clients, and ensure all active clients are bound to restrictive access policies with short-lived tokens. (Note: Modifying or deleting an active API client will immediately invalidate its issued tokens, so changes should be coordinated with the teams responsible for those integrations). From the GUI: ; Navigate to Settings > Access > Users and Policies. ; In the API Clients panel, select any unused clients and click the trash icon to delete them. ; For active clients, click the edit icon to reduce the assigned access policy or shorten the token TTL as appropriate.

title: Ensure static REST API tokens are used only when necessary and configured to expire periodically
description: FlashArray supports administrators creating static API for REST API access. This should only be utilized in cases where OAuth usage is not feasible. Everpure recommends the following: ; REST API tokens can be configured to expire. If REST API tokens are configured, configure them to expire periodically. Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.9 Ensure static REST API tokens are used only when necessary and configured to expire periodically

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Run the command pureadmin list --api-token to list all accounts and their API token status. ; Review the Created and Expires columns to identify tokens that lack an expiration date (indicated by a -) or have existed longer than the organization's rotation policy allows. ; Verify that each token-holding account is assigned the minimum required management access policy.

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, delete unauthorized or stale API tokens, and ensure that any newly issued tokens are configured with a strict validity period (timeout) so they expire automatically. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Settings > Access > Users and Policies. ; In the Users panel, click the Edit icon for the user you want to modify. ; To delete a token: Select Remove API Token... and click Remove to confirm. ; To rotate or create an expiring token: Select Create API Token... (or Recreate API Token... to overwrite an existing one). In the prompt, enter a validity period in the Expires In field so the token does not live indefinitely, then click Create. From the CLI:

title: Ensure administrative audit logs are forwarded to remote syslog or monitored via the REST API
description: FlashArray creates administrative audit records for all administrative operations that cause a change to the system configuration or state. Everpure recommends that these logs be monitored via REST API, or sent to configured remote syslog servers in order to detect suspicious or unexpected activity and respond accordingly. Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.10 Ensure administrative audit logs are forwarded to remote syslog or monitored via the REST API

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Verify Syslog Forwarding: Run the command purelog syslog list. Review the output to confirm a remote syslog server URI is configured. ; Verify Audit Records: Run the command pureaudit list (or pureaudit list -- filter "time >= '<YYYY-MM-DD>'" for recent events). Review the output to ensure the Time, User, Command, and Arguments are being accurately recorded. ; Verify REST API (If Syslog is not used): Verify with your monitoring teams that an active external script or tool is successfully authenticating and pulling the audit logs via the FlashArray REST API.

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, implement continuous monitoring by configuring external syslog forwarding or REST API integration, and establish a process to review unexpected configurations. From the GUI: ; To Configure Syslog Forwarding: ; Navigate to Settings > System. ; In the Syslog Servers panel, click the + (Create) icon. ; Enter the URI of your remote syslog server (e.g., tcp://10.10.10.10:514) and click Create. ; To Configure REST API Monitoring: ; Integrate your SIEM or monitoring tool using the Pure Storage REST API endpoints to continuously poll for audit trail events.

title: Ensure administrative session logs are forwarded to remote syslog or monitored via the REST API
description: FlashArray creates administrative session records for all administrative logins and logouts, whether successful or unsuccessful. Everpure recommends that these logs be monitored via REST API, or sent to configured remote syslog servers in order to detect suspicious or unexpected activity and respond accordingly. Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.11 Ensure administrative session logs are forwarded to remote syslog or monitored via the REST API

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Verify Session Records: Run the command puresession list to display user session logs. Review the output to ensure Start Time, End Time, Interface, User, Location, and Event fields are being actively recorded. ; Verify Syslog Forwarding: Run the command purelog syslog list to confirm a remote syslog server URI is configured. ; Verify REST API (If Syslog is not used): Verify with your monitoring teams that an external script is successfully polling the FlashArray REST API for session records.

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, implement continuous monitoring by configuring external syslog forwarding or REST API integration for session logs, and establish a process to review logs for weak authentication methods or unexpected access. From the GUI: ; Establish a Review Process: Create a standard operating procedure to regularly review the Session Log pane under Settings > Access specifically looking for unexpected IP locations or failed authentication events. ; To Configure Syslog Forwarding: Navigate to Settings > System. In the Syslog Servers panel, click the + (Create) icon, enter your remote syslog server URI, and click Create.

title: Ensure system alerts are actively monitored via remote syslog or email alert watchers
description: FlashArray creates alerts for a variety of system conditions that may be cause for concern. Not all of these are security related, but a number of them are either directly security related or can have an impact on security. Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.12 Ensure system alerts are actively monitored via remote syslog or email alert watchers

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Verify Alert Watchers (Email): Run the command purealert watcher list. Review the output to ensure that an internal organization email address is configured and enabled to receive notifications. ; Verify Syslog Forwarding: Run the command purelog syslog list. Review the output to confirm that a remote syslog server URI is actively configured to receive events (which includes purity.alert records).

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, implement a continuous alerting process by configuring an email alert watcher or remote syslog forwarding (or both). From the GUI: ; To Configure Alert Watchers (Email): ; Navigate to Settings > System and select Alerts and Notifications in the navigation pane. ; Add the appropriate internal email address for your organization's monitoring or administrative team to receive alert notifications. ; To Configure Syslog Forwarding: ; Navigate to Settings > System. ; In the Syslog Servers panel, create a syslog server by entering the URI of your remote syslog server (e.g., tcp://10.10.10.10:514) and saving the configuration. From the CLI:

title: Ensure at least one alert watcher is configured to receive alerts of all severities
description: FlashArray allows configuration of one or more alert watchers, which are email addresses that will receive emails for new system alerts. The minimum severity of alerts that will be sent to each watcher is also configurable. Passes when an enabled alert watcher other than the built-in purestorage.com address exists and a watcher rule sets Minimum Notification Severity to info. The audit is a config_regex check against a text export of the Purity//FA CLI, supplied with --device-config. Capture it over SSH with the --nvp (name=value) output option, for example: ssh pureuser@<array> "purealert watcher list --nvp; purepolicy alert-watcher rule list --nvp" > flasharray.txt (one file may hold the output of all commands used by this pack).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.13 Ensure at least one alert watcher is configured to receive alerts of all severities

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, configure an organizational email address to monitor array alerts. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Settings > System and select Alerts and Notifications. ; In the Alert Watchers panel, click the + (Create) icon, enter the desired email address, and click Create. ; To adjust the notification level, click the More Options menu next to the newly created watcher, select Edit, choose the minimum severity, and click Save. ; Ensure the Enabled switch is toggled on. From the CLI: ; Create the watcher: Run the purealert watcher create command. ; Command Syntax: purealert watcher create <EMAIL_ADDRESS>

title: Ensure at least one remote management syslog server is configured
description: FlashArray allows the creation of management syslog servers. These servers receive messages for administrative audit logs, administrative session logs, and alerts. Everpure recommends that you configure at least 1 management syslog server. Passes when at least one remote syslog server URI (udp://, tcp:// or tls://) is configured. The audit is a config_regex check against a text export of the Purity//FA CLI, supplied with --device-config. Capture it over SSH with the --nvp (name=value) output option, for example: ssh pureuser@<array> "purelog syslog list --nvp" > flasharray.txt (one file may hold the output of all commands used by this pack).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.14 Ensure at least one remote management syslog server is configured

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, configure at least one management syslog server to allow for real-time detection and response to unexpected events. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Settings > System. ; In the Syslog Servers panel, click the + (Create) icon. ; Enter the URI of your remote syslog server (e.g., tls://10.10.10.10:6514) and provide a name. ; Click Create to apply the configuration. From the CLI: ; Configure a remote syslog server destination using the purelog syslog create command. ; Command Syntax: purelog syslog create --uri <URI> <NAME> ; Example: purelog syslog create --uri tls://10.10.10.10:6514 syslog-server01

title: Ensure array TLS certificates are CA-signed, adequately sized, and rotated at least every 90 days
description: FlashArray allows certificates on the system to be centrally managed. This includes both "array-type" certificates, which the FlashArray storage array can use to represent itself to clients, and "external-type" certificates which can be the public certificates of certificate authorities that sign the certificates of other environmental resources or the public certificates of ... Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1 Ensure array TLS certificates are CA-signed, adequately sized, and rotated at least every 90 days

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Run the command purecert list to display the active certificates on the array. ; Review the output to ensure the following for your array type certificates: ; The Issuer is a trusted Certificate Authority. ; The Key Size is at least 2048 (for RSA) or 256 (for ECDSA). ; The difference between the Valid From and Valid To dates does not exceed 90 days. ; Verify that roots of trust are explicitly stored and listed under the external Type.

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, generate a properly sized Certificate Signing Request (CSR), have it signed by your CA for a maximum of 90 days, import it, and manage your roots of trust using external certificates. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Settings > System and locate the SSL Certificate / Array Certificates panel. ; Click the menu icon and select Construct Certificate Signing Request. Fill in the required attributes and ensure the key size meets the 2048-bit RSA or 256-bit ECDSA minimums. Click Create and download the CSR. ; Submit the CSR to your organization's trusted Certificate Authority and request that the signed certificate has a lifetime of 90 days or less.

title: Ensure Active Directory accounts are configured to require TLS
description: FlashArray supports native integration with Active Directory domains in order to enable LDAP lookups for authorization, and Kerberos authentication. FlashArray does this by creating a computer account in the domain to represent itself and generate kerberos keys. A unique AD account may be created for each server on the array that needs one. Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.3 Ensure Active Directory accounts are configured to require TLS

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Run the command puread account list to display information about Active Directory account attributes. ; Review the output and verify that the TLS column for the configured AD account is set to required (rather than optional).

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, update your Active Directory account configuration to explicitly require TLS for all domain controller communications. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Settings > Access > Users and Policies or Storage > Servers depending on where the AD account is applied. ; Edit the Active Directory configuration (e.g., in the Configure Remote Directory Service window). ; Under the TLS Mode setting, select the required radio button to force TLS communication with the domain controller. ; Click Create (or Save) to apply the configuration. From the CLI: ; Update the Active Directory account to require TLS using the puread account setattr command.

title: Ensure LDAP directory services use LDAPS with a configured CA root of trust
description: FlashArray supports LDAP directory services for administrative login and authorization, as well as for NFS authorization. Everpure recommends the following: ; Utilize LDAPS in order to establish secure LDAP connections. ; Specify one or more certificate authorities as roots of trust for each LDAP directory service. Fails when any directory service URI uses plaintext ldap://; also confirm a CA certificate is configured (pureds list --ca-certificate). Passes when no directory service is configured (see 1.2). The audit is a config_regex check against a text export of the Purity//FA CLI, supplied with --device-config. Capture it over SSH with the --nvp (name=value) output option, for example: ssh pureuser@<array> "pureds list --nvp; pureds list --ca-certificate" > flasharray.txt (one file may hold the output of all commands used by this pack).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.4 Ensure LDAP directory services use LDAPS with a configured CA root of trust

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, update your directory service configuration to enforce LDAPS and configure the appropriate CA certificate for trust. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Settings > Access > Users and Policies. ; In the Directory Service panel, select either the Array Management or Data button, then click the edit icon. ; Update the URIs field to use the ldaps:// scheme (e.g., ldaps://ldap.company.com:636) and click Save. ; To configure the root of trust, click Edit next to CA Certificate within the Directory Service panel. Paste the PEM-formatted certificate from your Certificate Authority and click Save.

title: Ensure syslog servers use TLS with a configured CA root of trust
description: FlashArray supports configuring remote syslog servers to receive a variety of different messages, including administrative and data audit records, session records, and alerts. Everpure recommends the following: ; Configure all syslog servers to use TLS to protect traffic from inspection and tampering. Fails when any syslog server URI uses udp:// or tcp:// instead of tls://; also confirm a syslog CA certificate is imported. 1.14 covers the case where no syslog server exists. The audit is a config_regex check against a text export of the Purity//FA CLI, supplied with --device-config. Capture it over SSH with the --nvp (name=value) output option, for example: ssh pureuser@<array> "purelog syslog list --nvp; purelog syslog global list --ca-certificate" > flasharray.txt (one file may hold the output of all commands used by this pack).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.5 Ensure syslog servers use TLS with a configured CA root of trust

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, configure your syslog servers to use TLS encryption and import a CA certificate to authenticate the remote servers. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Settings > System. ; In the Syslog Servers panel, remove any existing plaintext syslog entries. ; Enter the URI of your remote syslog server using the tls:// scheme (e.g., tls://10.10.10.10:6514). ; Click the Add button to add the URI to the list of syslog server output locations. From the CLI: ; Delete the existing plaintext syslog server: ; Command Syntax: purelog syslog delete <SERVER_NAME> ; Add a TLS-encrypted syslog server:

title: Ensure the SMTP relay host is configured with STARTTLS encryption and authentication
description: FlashArray supports configuring a relayhost for the simple mail transfer protocol (SMTP) for the purpose of ensuring email delivery for alert emails. Everpure recommends the following: ; Configure an SMTP relayhost. ; Configure the starttls encryption mode for SMTP. Passes when a relay host is configured and Encryption Mode is starttls; confirm a Username is set when the relay requires authentication. The audit is a config_regex check against a text export of the Purity//FA CLI, supplied with --device-config. Capture it over SSH with the --nvp (name=value) output option, for example: ssh pureuser@<array> "puresmtp list --nvp" > flasharray.txt (one file may hold the output of all commands used by this pack).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.6 Ensure the SMTP relay host is configured with STARTTLS encryption and authentication

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, update your SMTP configuration to specify your relay host, enforce TLS encryption, and configure authentication credentials. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Settings > System and locate the Alert Routing (Relay Host) panel. ; Enter your SMTP Relay Host address. ; Set the Encryption Mode to starttls. ; If authentication is required, enter the Username and Password. ; Click Save. From the CLI: ; Configure the relay host and enforce TLS: Use the puresmtp setattr command to specify your server and set the encryption mode to starttls. ; Command Syntax: puresmtp setattr --relay-host <HOST> --encryption- mode starttls

title: Ensure SNMP, if enabled, uses SNMPv3 with SHA authentication and AES privacy
description: FlashArray supports configuring the simple network management protocol (SNMP). An SNMP agent can be configured on the array, allowing external clients to query the array using SNMP for information such as performance metrics and array details. SNMP managers can also be configured to receive alerts. Fails when the SNMP agent (localhost) or any manager uses v1/v2c, MD5 authentication or DES privacy; confirm v3 with SHA and AES and passphrases of 8+ characters. The audit is a config_regex check against a text export of the Purity//FA CLI, supplied with --device-config. Capture it over SSH with the --nvp (name=value) output option, for example: ssh pureuser@<array> "puresnmp list --nvp" > flasharray.txt (one file may hold the output of all commands used by this pack).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.7 Ensure SNMP, if enabled, uses SNMPv3 with SHA authentication and AES privacy

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, update your SNMP configuration to utilize SNMPv3 with strong authentication and privacy protocols, and ensure passphrases meet the 8-character minimum complexity requirement. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Settings > System. ; In the SNMP panel, click the menu icon and select Add SNMP Manager (or click Edit for an existing manager). ; Complete the following fields in the dialog box: ; SNMP Version: Select v3. ; User: Enter the recognized User ID. ; Auth Protocol: Select SHA. ; Auth Passphrase: Enter a complex passphrase of at least 8 characters. ; Privacy Protocol: Select AES. ; Privacy Passphrase: Enter a complex passphrase of at least 8 characters.

title: Ensure product diagnostic tests for environmental integrations are run periodically
description: For many environmental integrations mentioned in this section, there exists FlashArray functionality to detect that your configuration is still working. Everpure recommends that you periodically run the product diagnostics tests for the following configurations: ; SAML ; LDAP ; Active Directory ; Syslog ; SMTP Email delivery to alert watchers ; SNMP delivery to SNMP managers Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.9 Ensure product diagnostic tests for environmental integrations are run periodically

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Request evidence from your monitoring or automation teams that a script periodically connects to the array to execute configuration test commands (e.g., puresso saml2 test, pureds test, purelog syslog test, purealert watcher test, and purearray test ntp).

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, implement an automated script or a manual maintenance schedule to continuously verify that environmental integrations are fully functional. From the GUI: ; Establish a periodic manual review process to execute available GUI diagnostic tests. ; Test Directory Services: Navigate to Settings > Access > Users and Policies. In the Directory Service panel, click Test to verify that URIs resolve and the array can bind to the LDAP/AD tree. ; Test SAML2 SSO: Navigate to Settings > Access > Users and Policies.

title: Ensure native Active Directory integration is used for NFS and SMB identity and authentication
description: FlashArray supports native integration with Active Directory domains in order to enable LDAP lookups for authorization, and Kerberos authentication, for both NFS and SMB file access. FlashArray does this by creating a computer account in the domain to represent itself and generate kerberos keys. A unique AD account may be created for each server on the array that needs one. Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.3 Ensure native Active Directory integration is used for NFS and SMB identity and authentication

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Check the Active Directory domain join status by running the command puread account list. ; Review the output to verify that your file server's AD account is listed and the Domain field is correct.

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, join the FlashArray file server to your Active Directory domain. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Storage > Servers and click your file server to access its settings. ; In the Remote Directory Service panel, click the Edit Configuration icon to the right and select Active Directory. ; In the Configure Remote Directory Service window, enter a Name, the Domain DNS Name, and the Computer Name for the array. ; Enter the AD User and AD Password for an Active Directory account with permission to create a new computer account (or select the Use Existing Account toggle if pre-created by your AD admin). ; Ensure TLS Mode is set to required.

title: Ensure space consumption and performance are monitored for anomalies
description: FlashArray offers capabilities for monitoring space consumption, data reduction, and performance across a variety of axes. For performance, these include, but are not limited to: ; Array-wide ; By directory ; By volume ; By volume group ; By host ; By host group For space, these include, but are not limited to: ; Array-wide ; By directory ; By volume ; By volume group Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.5 Ensure space consumption and performance are monitored for anomalies

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Check file system / directory space usage by running the command puredir list --space. ; Check real-time or historical array performance metrics by running the command purearray monitor (or purearray monitor --historical <TIME>). ; Check array-wide space usage by running the command purearray list -- space.

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, implement a regular monitoring process using the built-in Analysis dashboards or automated CLI scripts to track capacity and performance trends. From the GUI: ; Establish a continuous manual monitoring routine using the Analysis > Capacity and Analysis > Performance pages to monitor capacity trends and bandwidth/IOPS metrics. ; Ensure you have configured syslog servers or email alert watchers (as covered in earlier sections) so that built-in capacity alerts (e.g., warnings when storage consumption reaches 90% of usable capacity) are proactively pushed to your monitoring teams. From the CLI:

title: Ensure SMB audit policies with syslog and file log targets are attached to production file systems
description: FlashArray supports creation of one or more audit policies for enabling audit of operations over the SMB data protocol. These audit policies may be used to send audit records to remote syslog servers for monitoring. Everpure recommends the following: ; Configure at least 1 syslog server and 1 directory as log targets among your audit policies for SMB. Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.6 Ensure SMB audit policies with syslog and file log targets are attached to production file systems

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Run the commands purelog file list and purelog syslog list to verify that local and remote log targets exist. ; Run the command purepolicy audit file list to verify that an audit policy exists and its Enabled status is set to True. ; Review the policy members by running purepolicy audit file list --member to ensure the policies are successfully attached to the correct source managed directories.

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, establish file log targets, create an audit policy, attach it to your production managed directories, and externally configure SACLs for SMB exports. From the GUI: ; Create the File Log Target: Navigate to Settings > System. In the File Log Targets panel, click the + (Create) icon. Provide a name, select an empty managed directory to store the logs, configure a retention policy (Keep For or Keep Size), and click Create. ; Create the Syslog Target (if not already configured): In the Syslog Servers panel, add your remote syslog server URI. ; Create the Audit Policy: Navigate to Storage > Policies.

title: Ensure production volumes and hosts are protected by ratcheted (SafeMode) protection groups with daily snapshots
description: FlashArray allows for protection groups (pgroups) to be created. These pgroups can be attached to hosts and volumes in order to schedule the creation and replication of snapshots for the purpose of data protection. Additionally, pgroups may be ratcheted to enable a feature known as SafeMode. Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2 Ensure production volumes and hosts are protected by ratcheted (SafeMode) protection groups with daily snapshots

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Run the commands purevol list --protect (and purehost list --protect) to verify that your production workloads are actively associated with a protection group. ; Run the command purepgroup list --retention-lock to verify the SafeMode status is ratcheted for your production protection groups. ; Run the commands purepgroup list --schedule and purepgroup list -- retention to verify that the snapshot and replication frequencies are at least daily and retained for at least 7 days.

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, create a volume-based protection group, establish daily snapshot and replication schedules with at least 7 days of retention, and ratchet the group to enable SafeMode. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Protection > Protection Groups. ; In the Source Protection Groups panel, click the + (Create Protection Group) icon, enter a name, and click Create. ; Click on the newly created protection group to open its details. ; In the Members pane, click the menu icon, select Add..., select your production volumes, and click Add. ; In the Snapshot Schedule and Replication Schedule panes, click the Edit (pen and paper) icon.

title: Ensure an enabled snapshot policy taking at least one daily snapshot is attached to every directory
description: FlashArray supports creating snapshot policies for automatically creating, managing, and deleting immutable snapshots of FlashArray directories. These policies can be additionally used to replicate file snapshots. Everpure recommends the following if you have any file systems on the system: ; Attach at least one enabled snapshot policy to each directory. Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.3 Ensure an enabled snapshot policy taking at least one daily snapshot is attached to every directory

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Run the command purepolicy snapshot rule list to verify the configured rules on your snapshot policies. ; Review the output to ensure the frequency (every) is at least daily (1d) and the retention (keep_for) is at least 7 days (7d or 1w). ; Run the command purepolicy snapshot list --member to view all configured snapshot policies and verify that your production managed directories are successfully attached to them.

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, establish a snapshot policy that takes daily snapshots with a 7-day retention period, and attach it to your file system managed directories. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Protection > Policies. ; In the Snapshot Policies panel, click the + (Create Policy) icon. Provide a name, ensure the Enabled toggle is active (blue), and click Create. ; Click on the newly created policy name to open its details. ; In the Rules panel, click the + (Create Rule) icon (or menu icon > Create...) to add a new rule. ; Set Create 1 snapshot every to 1d (or a shorter interval like 12h). ; Set And keep for to 1w (or 7d or a longer duration like 30d).

title: Ensure default protection is configured at the array level and for every pod
description: FlashArray allows the array and its pods to have default protection configured. This allows you to configure pgroups that will be automatically associated with any volumes created within the pod or the array. This can be used to ensure that all block data has some level of data protection by default. Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.4 Ensure default protection is configured at the array level and for every pod

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Run the command purearray default-protection list to view the default protection group lists for the array root (denoted by - in the Container Name column) and all pods. ; Run the command purepgroup list --retention-lock to verify that the SafeMode status is ratcheted and manual eradication is disabled for the protection groups assigned as defaults.

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, assign a ratcheted protection group to the array root and all pods so that newly provisioned data receives baseline SafeMode protection automatically. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Protection > Array. ; In the Default Protection panel, click the Edit (Set Default Protection) icon on the right of the appropriate row (the - row for the root of the array, or the row for a specific pod). ; In the Available Protection Groups column, select the protection groups to be added so they appear in the Selected Protection Groups column. ; Click Set. ; Navigate to Protection > Protection Groups and select your assigned default protection group.

title: Ensure at least one encrypted array connection is configured for replication
description: FlashArray allows for connections to be created between any 2 FlashArrays for the purpose of replicating block and file data asynchronously, or block data synchronously. This allows for backups of data to be copied to other arrays, enabling disaster recovery. FlashArray supports creating pods and using them to store file and block data to coordinate replication. Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.5 Ensure at least one encrypted array connection is configured for replication

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Run the command purearray connection list to view the status and attributes of connected arrays. ; Review the output to ensure that a connection exists, the Transport is ip, and Encryption is set to encrypted. ; Run the purevol list --protect and purefs list commands to verify that all storage objects are associated with a replicating protection group or pod.

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, establish an encrypted array connection using an encrypted pre-shared key, and ensure your production data is actively replicating. From the GUI: ; Get the Connection Key: Log in to the target array, navigate to Protection > Array, click the menu icon in the Connected Arrays panel, and select Create Encrypted Connection Key. Copy the key. ; Connect the Arrays: Log in to the source array, navigate to Protection > Array, click the menu icon in the Connected Arrays panel, and select Connect Array.

title: Ensure the health of array connections and offload targets is continuously monitored
description: Whether utilizing array connections or offload targets, FlashArray periodically monitors them for health issues that impact your ability to backup data. Everpure recommends that you monitor the health of your array connections and offload targets, in order to detect unhealthy statuses. Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.7 Ensure the health of array connections and offload targets is continuously monitored

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Run the command purearray connection list to verify the status of peer array connections. ; Run the command purepod replica-link list to verify the status of ActiveDR connections. ; Run the command pureoffload list to display all connected offload targets. ; Review the outputs to ensure the paths are healthy and not displaying a connecting, quarantined, or unhealthy state.

remediation.command: Because this is a continuous monitoring procedure, remediation involves establishing regular manual or automated review processes to track connection metrics and respond to anomalies. From the GUI (for manual monitoring): ; Navigate to Protection > Array. ; In the Connected Arrays panel, monitor the Status column. A status of connecting indicates an unhealthy connection (typically due to network issues), while quarantined indicates an unstable synchronous replication path that has been temporarily embargoed. ; In the Offload Targets panel, monitor the Status column.

title: Ensure SAML SSO uses HTTPS with encrypted assertions and signed requests
description: SAML may be used for delegated authentication across various protocols on FlashArray. The array URL, IDP metadata URL, and IDP URL are all required to use https if specified. IDP Metadata URL usage is optional; if one is not used, then you may instead manually configure the IDP URL, verification certificate, and IDP entity ID. Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.2 Ensure SAML SSO uses HTTPS with encrypted assertions and signed requests

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Display the full SAML2 SSO configuration and certificate details by running the command puresso saml2 list --verification-certificate. ; Review the output to confirm that the Array URL and IdP URL fields begin with https://. ; Verify that the Sign Request and Encrypt Assertion attributes are set to True. ; Review the Verification Certificate details to ensure it was issued by a trusted CA and the Valid To date is not expired.

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, update your SAML2 SSO configuration to require HTTPS, signed requests, and encrypted assertions using dedicated credentials. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Settings > Access > Users and Policies and scroll to the SAML2 SSO pane. ; Click the edit icon for the Configuration. ; Update the Array URL and IdP URL fields to ensure they begin with https://. ; Enable Signed Requests: Slide the Sign Request toggle to the right (blue) and enter your array's signing certificate name in the Signing Credential field.

title: Ensure at least 3 NTP servers and an NTP symmetric key are configured
description: The network time protocol (NTP) allows time to be synchronized between devices on a network. Everpure recommends the following: ; Configure at least 3 NTP servers. ; Configure an NTP symmetric key. Note: The NTP symmetric key cannot be configured through the GUI. This can only be done through the CLI. Passes when at least three comma-separated NTP servers and an NTP symmetric key are configured. The audit is a config_regex check against a text export of the Purity//FA CLI, supplied with --device-config. Capture it over SSH with the --nvp (name=value) output option, for example: ssh pureuser@<array> "purearray list --ntp --nvp" > flasharray.txt (one file may hold the output of all commands used by this pack).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.8 Ensure at least 3 NTP servers and an NTP symmetric key are configured

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, configure at least three NTP servers and secure the communication using an NTP symmetric key. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Settings > System. ; In the Time panel, locate the NTP Servers section. ; In the New NTP Server(s) text box, type the hostname or IP address of your NTP servers (you can enter multiple servers as comma-separated values). ; Click the Add button. Ensure you have added at least three servers. From the CLI: ; Configure at least three NTP servers: Specify the servers using the purearray setattr command. ; Command Syntax: purearray setattr --ntpserver <SERVER1>,<SERVER2>,<SERVER3>

title: Ensure a hard-limit quota policy is enforced on the root managed directory of every file system
description: FlashArray supports configuring quota policies in order to enforce space consumption limits on directories. These allow you to limit the total amount of space any directory and its child files and directories can consume. Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.4 Ensure a hard-limit quota policy is enforced on the root managed directory of every file system

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Run the command puredir quota list to display all directories with an attached quota policy. Verify that the root managed directories for your file systems are listed. ; Run the command purepolicy quota rule list to inspect the rules for the attached policies. Verify that the Enforced column is set to True and an appropriate Quota Limit is established.

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, create a quota policy with an enforced hard limit and attach it to the root managed directory of each file system. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Storage > Policies. ; In the Quota Policies panel, click the + (Create Policy) icon. ; In the pop-up window, enter a Name for the policy. ; In the rules section, specify the Quota Limit (e.g., 5T). ; Click the Enabled toggle icon next to Enforced so that it turns blue. This ensures new writes are blocked when the limit is exceeded. Click Create. ; Click the name of your newly created quota policy. ; In the Members panel, click the menu icon and select Add Member.

title: Ensure a snapshot offload target using HTTPS is configured when no array connection is available
description: FlashArray allows for connections to be created between a FlashArray and a generic offload target. Offload targets allow snapshots to be stored externally to the array, with storage and transmission of proprietary-format snapshots via standardized 3rd party protocols. Offload targets can either utilize the S3 data format, such as Amazon AWS, or the Azure blob format. Manual review in the Purity//FA GUI or CLI (organization-specific or per-object evidence).
reference: CIS Everpure FlashArray Purity 6.9.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.6 Ensure a snapshot offload target using HTTPS is configured when no array connection is available

audit.command: From the CLI: ; Run the command pureoffload list to display all connected offload targets and their general statuses. ; Run pureoffload s3 list or pureoffload azure list to display detailed connection settings. ; Review the output to ensure the connection exists and that any defined URI uses the https:// protocol rather than http://.

remediation.command: To align with the security recommendations, establish an offload target to act as a secondary backup repository and ensure secure transmission by enforcing HTTPS for any custom endpoints. From the GUI: ; Navigate to Protection > Array. ; In the Offload Targets panel, click the + (connect) icon. ; In the Connect Offload Target window, select the Protocol (s3 or azure). ; For Azure Blob: Type a target Name, the Microsoft Azure Account name, the Container name, and the Secret Access Key. ; For S3: Type a target Name, the AWS Access Key ID, the Bucket name, and the Secret Access Key. ; If a custom endpoint/URI is required, ensure it begins with https://.
